title: Level 3 Business Studies — Global Business Context 2025
subject: business-studies

questions.text:
Background: Tōtara Outdoor Gear is a New Zealand-registered business that has been designing and manufacturing outdoor clothing and equipment for over twenty years. They export to 45 countries, with strongest sales growth in Scandinavia. In 2023, Tōtara expanded to Norway but sales have been lower than expected. They are now considering withdrawing from Norway.

(a)(i) Explain one possible reason for sales of Tōtara's products being lower than expected in Norway.

(a)(ii) Explain the effect the lower than expected sales in Norway may have on Tōtara's profit.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Explain one possible reason for lower sales (State the reason, then expand).
- E.g.
- Norwegian consumers already have strong loyalty to established local outdoor brands such as Bergans and Norrøna, making it difficult for a new entrant to gain market share.
- For profit: The lower-than-expected sales may have a negative impact on Tōtara's profit.
- Marketing and distribution costs were budgeted assuming higher sales volumes would cover them.
- With costs as expected but revenue lower, profits will be below target.

For Merit:
- Fully explain with further expansion of how this could impact business or stakeholder goals.

For Excellence:
- Justify by using relevant evidence including reference to alternative courses of action.

questions.text:
Another challenge Tōtara is facing in Scandinavia is that their products are not always reaching stores quickly enough. Customers often find the products they want are out of stock.

(b)(i) Explain one possible reason for Tōtara's products not reaching stores quickly enough.

(b)(ii) Explain the effect that stock shortages may have on Tōtara's market share.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Explain one possible cause, e.g.
- the long shipping distance from New Zealand to Scandinavia.
- Sea freight takes approximately 35-40 days, and seasonal demand for outdoor gear can spike unpredictably, meaning stock orders placed months in advance may not match actual demand.
- For market share: Stock shortages will likely decrease Tōtara's market share.
- When customers cannot find Tōtara products, they will purchase from a competing brand.
- If unavailability becomes regular, retailers may reduce shelf space allocated to Tōtara and consumers may switch permanently, further reducing sales and market share.

For Merit:
- Fully explain with further expansion.

For Excellence:
- Justify by evaluating and integrating detailed evidence.

questions.text:
Tōtara is considering moving their European distribution centre from Copenhagen, Denmark to Amsterdam in the Netherlands. If they move, they will ship directly to Amsterdam's port rather than via Copenhagen.

(c)(i) Explain one advantage to Tōtara of moving their distribution centre to Amsterdam.

(c)(ii) Explain one disadvantage to Tōtara of moving their distribution centre to Amsterdam.

(c)(iii) Would you recommend that Tōtara move their distribution centre to Amsterdam? Justify your recommendation, including any new information.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Explain one advantage (e.g.
- Amsterdam's port is one of Europe's largest, with more frequent shipping connections to New Zealand and faster customs processing, reducing delivery lead times) and one disadvantage (e.g.
- higher warehouse rental costs in Amsterdam's competitive logistics market — approximately $32,000 per year more than Copenhagen).

For Merit:
- Fully explain with further expansion about effects, advantages, disadvantages.

For Excellence:
- For the recommendation, justify using relevant evidence.
- E.g.
- Tōtara should move because Amsterdam provides better connectivity to the UK, Germany, and France — their largest European markets — and the port's efficiency would reduce delivery times by an estimated week.
- The increased lease costs would be offset by reduced shipping fees and fewer lost sales from stock shortages.
- Note: A recommendation for staying in Copenhagen is acceptable if suitably justified.

questions.text:
Tōtara is considering purchasing new fabric cutting equipment to replace their current machines. They have two options: Machine A (laser cutter, $68,000, cuts 200 panels per hour, minimal waste at 3%, staff training cost $18,000) and Machine B (automated blade cutter, $45,000, cuts 150 panels per hour, waste at 8%, staff training cost $7,500).

(d)(i) Explain one benefit to Tōtara of purchasing Machine A.

(d)(ii) Explain one benefit to Tōtara of purchasing Machine B.

(d)(iii) Which of the two cutting machine options would you recommend for Tōtara? Justify your recommendation, including any new information.
questions.markingGuide:
WHAT YOU NEED TO INCLUDE:

For Achievement:
- Explain one benefit of Machine A (e.g.
- much less fabric waste at 3% vs 8%, saving material costs and supporting environmental sustainability goals) and one benefit of Machine B (e.g.
- lower total upfront cost of $52,500 vs $86,000, preserving working capital).

For Merit:
- Fully explain with further expansion of how the benefits impact business or stakeholder goals.

For Excellence:
- For the recommendation, justify using relevant evidence.
- E.g.
- Tōtara should purchase Machine A because the 5% reduction in fabric waste would save approximately $15,000-$20,000 per year on material costs, recouping the higher purchase price within 2-3 years.
- Machine A's higher output rate of 200 vs 150 panels per hour would also help address the stock shortage problem in Scandinavia.
- Note: A recommendation for Machine B is acceptable if suitably justified.
